why: The new fallback ordering that prefers keeping short function words attached to their following head made the model avoid single-word fragments, which raised H_set for short-latency pieces (positive means in ≤3/≤5/≤7/≤10 bins) but shifted cut choices in longer sentences (slight negative for ≤99 and several large degradations), e.g. moving cuts into or out of quoted complements and splitting enumerations.
lesson: A later revision should preserve the fallback’s clear benefit for very short pieces while avoiding broad application that repositions top cuts in long sentences and thereby breaks enumerations or quoted complements.
